text:
olivia: Follow-up from RFC: we hit a weird fairness flip when a tenant had reserved tokens in parallel regions. Wants a lightweight inter-region handshake so two regions don't both briefly believe they have headroom.

ben: Can you summarize the user impact? Is this causing hard rejects or just degraded latency?

olivia: Mostly unfair scheduling -> tenant saw higher concurrency in eu causing others in us to be throttled. No permanent token leak but a 10-15s window where requests were over-provisioned. Users saw increased 429s downstream.

zoe: Evidence suggests race during leader handover + cross-region lease lag. Our current approach uses last-write-wins to balance but that's not enough for short cutovers.

sara: I'd propose an idempotent two-phase-ish approach for reservation updates: 1) tentative delta written to a lightweight idempotent reservo log replicated cross-region (append-only), 2) regions consult the log within a bounded window (e.g., 3s) before committing local quota state.

michael: Two-phase sounds heavy. Alternative: hedged reservations—first issue a short-lived provisional token (ttl=2s) locally and broadcast a commit message async. If commit ack doesn't arrive, tokens expire and compensator reclaims. Low latency at ingress, eventual correctness.

ben: Hedged provisional tokens are promising. We need an explicit ingress contract to avoid apps getting surprised. How about header `X-Quota-Phase: tentative|committed|finalize` so SDKs can surface to app logic and optionally retry with different routing logic.

olivia: +1 to that header idea. Also suggest we add `X-Quota-Reconcile-Id` GUID on the request path for tracing. We'll need trace joins in telemetry.

sara: Telemetry: emit events for provisional-token-issued, commit-ack, commit-miss, reclaim-action. Also metric `provisional_token_overlaps` to measure double-counting incidents.

michael: For storage, I'd keep the reservo log in our fast kv (region-local with async cross-region append). Use sequence numbers to avoid reordering issues.

zoe: Edge case: what if a region completely loses connectivity and provisional tokens accumulate? We should cap provisional tokens globally per-tenant (max_provisional_ratio, default 0.05 of committed). Also have a fast eviction path if connectivity down > 10s.

ben: Operationally: rollout plan -> feature flag hedged reservations, canary in eu-west, enable X-Quota-Phase for 10% of traffic (SDK/edge honors header), monitor provisional_token_overlaps and 429 spike. Abort if overlap rate > 0.1% or 429 increase > 5x baseline.

infra-bot: deploy: quota-hedge/v0.1 -> succeeded :rocket:

olivia: Owners & next steps: Ben -> RFC update w/ sequence diagrams; Sara -> telemetry dashboard (provisional overlap, reconcile latency, degraded tenants); Michael -> prototype hedged token store + TTL reclamation; Zoe -> storage layout and seqno semantics.

ben: I'll draft RFC and include sample gRPC handshake + error cases (commit missing, partial acks). Expect EOD Wednesday.

olivia: Thanks all — this feels lower-risk than full two-phase, keeps tail latency good and gives us observable signals to tune.

michael: One more thing: add a reconciliation healthcheck endpoint that returns outstanding provisional counts per-tenant so ops can script emergency drains.

zoe: noted. I'll add schema for the healthcheck response and layout for seqno trimming.

ben: Cool. Will include abort criteria and perf baseline in RFC. :thumbsup:
